title: Issue 6: structured logging and error visibility

requirements.expectation: Current payment/job logging, empty catches, and error responses are inventoried with deliberate fallback and typed-error behavior distinguished from swallowed failures.
requirements.verification: Recount targeted paths and trace relevant callers; document baseline and explicitly excluded cases.

requirements.expectation: API requests receive a validated or generated request ID that is returned to clients and available to server logs across the relevant call chain.
requirements.verification: Test generated IDs, valid/invalid incoming IDs, response headers, context propagation, and parallel requests without cross-request leakage.
evidence: Middleware test confirms bounded supplied IDs are returned and invalid IDs are replaced by UUIDs; middleware also forwards the ID on the request.

requirements.expectation: Server events use a consistent JSON schema with severity, stable event name, timestamp, request ID when available, and safe error metadata.
requirements.verification: Unit-test serialization and required fields; inspect emitted output in server runtime; confirm browser code cannot import the server-only logger.
evidence: Focused tests confirm JSON shape, severity/event/request correlation fields, allowlisted context, and server logger output.

requirements.expectation: Logs exclude credentials, authorization headers, provider payloads, and unnecessary personal/payment data; stack traces and diagnostics remain server-side.
requirements.verification: Use sentinel secrets and representative provider/customer errors in tests; inspect serialized logs and API responses for leakage.
evidence: Focused tests confirm arbitrary context and untrusted exception messages are omitted; only allowlisted identifiers and error class/code metadata are serialized. Exception stacks are also omitted.

requirements.expectation: High-risk payment and job failures, including formerly swallowed failures, produce actionable structured events without changing transaction, retry, or fallback semantics.
requirements.verification: Review confirmation/refund/payout and job transition/retry/recovery call paths; test caught failures and verify one useful event with safe identifiers and request correlation where available.
evidence: Payment/job API route failures now emit stable events with allowlisted identifiers and generic 5xx responses; selected best-effort failures also log. Lower-level payment/job services still contain legacy console calls, and injected route/service failure tests remain outstanding.

requirements.expectation: Known typed/auth/validation errors retain intended public status and message; unknown internal failures return generic 5xx responses and are logged server-side.
requirements.verification: Test typed and unknown errors for scoped API routes; assert internal messages and stacks are absent from client responses.
evidence: apiFailFromError unit test confirms explicit typed 403 and 503 statuses are retained, typed client messages remain public, and 5xx details/codes map to generic responses. Scoped API catches return generic messages for unknown failures.

requirements.expectation: Observability changes preserve Issue 4 concurrency behavior and Issue 5 transactional/idempotent payment-job processing; out-of-scope client logs and intentional fallbacks are not mechanically altered.
requirements.verification: Run focused tests plus relevant payment/job regression suites; inspect diff for altered business outcomes and broad mechanical replacements.
evidence: Full test suite passes (102 files, 1,205 tests); typecheck passes. Diff review confirms changes are limited to middleware correlation, logger/error handling, docs, and focused tests.

requirements.expectation: A non-production hosted request can be correlated through the platform logs with the returned request ID, and log retention/access are understood.
requirements.verification: Record a sanitized request ID and matching hosted log evidence; document platform retention, access controls, and any truncation limits.

requirements.expectation: Sentry/OpenTelemetry adoption is either configured and verified or explicitly deferred with an owner and follow-up requirement.
requirements.verification: Document provider, environment configuration/secrets, sampling/privacy settings, alert ownership, and a non-production delivery test, or record the deferral decision.

implementationNotes: Middleware request ID propagation, server JSON logger with allowlisted context and no untrusted exception messages/stacks, generic 5xx error mapping, and API-level payment/job route migration are implemented locally. Full unit tests, typecheck, and lint pass. Lower-level service console migration and hosted log evidence remain pending.
implementationState: First API-level implementation is in progress; local checks pass, lower-level service coverage and release evidence pending

independentReview.scope: Review the implementation commit against each criterion, including privacy/redaction and typed-error compatibility.

code: Migrate remaining high-risk lower-level payment/job service console calls with safe context, and inventory residual catches/logging.
Add injected route/service failure tests and complete an independent review.
external: Verify request ID and JSON log correlation in non-production hosting; document retention, access controls, and alert ownership.
Decide whether to adopt Sentry/OpenTelemetry and record the configuration/test or explicit deferral.
